source_documents.title: Interrogating the Azo-Hydrazo Proton Transfer Process in the Excited State Using a Multipronged Spectroscopic Study: Effect of Annulation and Solvent

reference_evidence_units.quote: we infer that the ESIPT process in both PDNO and NDNO is considerably fast, occurring at a time scale less than 100 ps.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDNO, NDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Azo-to-hydrazo excited-state proton transfer is faster than 100 ps in both dyes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The azo and hydrazo tautomeric forms of PDNO and NDNO are present in the ground state; the thermally allowed conversion of the azo to the hydrazo form results in a very poor quantum yield of the dyes in solution phase.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDNO, NDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Both tautomers coexist in the ground state; the dyes are very weakly emissive.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The higher value of Stokes’ Shift for the 650 nm emission band supports the excited state tautomerization of the trans-azo form to the trans-hydrazo form, in keeping with literature reports.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: The large-Stokes-shift 650 nm band comes from the hydrazo tautomer formed in the excited state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Hence, the increasing contribution of the τ1 component at the red λobs leads us to assign it as the lifetime of deactivation of the trans-hydrazo-tautomer, as the ultrafast photo tautomerism yields the trans-hydrazo from the excited trans-azo form.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDNO, NDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: The short red-side lifetime belongs to the hydrazo tautomer formed by ultrafast phototautomerism.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The second extracted lifetime τ2 (with associated EADS 2), ranging between 5.0 and 12.0 ps, is plausibly assigned to trans-cis isomerization of the dyes, in line with previously reported studies on PDNO.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDNO, NDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: A 5-12 ps component is assigned to trans-cis isomerization.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Assignment by analogy to earlier PDNO work.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We attribute this difference based on the greater conjugation in NDNO due to the presence of an extra phenyl ring, which is reported to have slower relaxation pathways in organic dyes.
reference_evidence_units.subject: NDNO vs PDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: NDNO relaxes more slowly than PDNO in every solvent.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Thus, we could safely state that chloroform provides the optimal polarity and viscosity to reduce the rate of relaxation of the dyes.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PDNO, NDNO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Relaxation is slowest in chloroform; protic MeOH speeds nonradiative relaxation.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Same ultrafast azo-to-hydrazo ESIPT as PDNO; the extra ring slows the subsequent nonradiative relaxation.

environment_context: solvent: relaxation is slowest in chloroform and faster in protic methanol; the paper discusses a polarity/viscosity balance without a specific restricted motion (E07)
out_of_pool: PHOTOCHEMISTRY: trans-cis photoisomerization about the azo/hydrazo linkage (5-12 ps component) (E05)

contrast_group.varied_factor: aryl group on the azo nitrogen of 2-naphthol (phenyl vs 1-naphthyl)
contrast_group.paper_difference: Both show ultrafast azo-to-hydrazo ESIPT and very weak emission; the naphthyl dye NDNO has red-shifted bands and slower nonradiative relaxation than PDNO in every solvent.

basis: name 1-naphthylazo-2-naphthol in the paper, parsed with OPSIN (1-naphthyl)
trans-azo tautomer written as named; the paper reports azo and hydrazo tautomers together in the ground state
